tagline: A king dies. An era ends. You are the dreamer the crown chose.
voice: Medieval fantasy, mythic-grim. Sparse, weighty prose. Stakes are felt; magic costs.
settingAndTone: Medieval fantasy, mythic-grim. Sparse, weighty prose. Stakes are felt; magic costs.

structuralObjective.thematic: King Aldric dies. An era ends. The player is the catalyst — directly, indirectly, or through their absence. The path adapts to player choices; the objective does not.
structuralObjective.climaxTypeRaw: Succession (the dying king's power passes — to the player, to the antagonist, or to no one)

worldBible.geography: Kingdom of Vael. Capital: Vael's Reach (walled city, river-bend, royal keep). Wren's Hollow (player's village, 4 days west). Eastern Road (the corridor between). Dead Pines (forest, midway). Various villages along the road.
worldBible.magicTechRules: Magic exists but is rare and costly. The Ember Crown is a true relic — it cannot be lifted by anyone who has not dreamed of it (they burn). Dreams from the Crown are real prophetic events, not metaphor. No teleportation, no resurrection, no instant communication.
worldBible.factions: The Old Faction (loyal to Aldric, want legitimate succession). Halric's Faction (planning to crown a puppet). The Temple (technically neutral but compromised). The Bandit Clans (chaotic, opportunistic). The dreaming bloodline (the player and rare others).
worldBible.recentHistory: Aldric has reigned 22 years — a stable golden age after a long civil war. The Ember Crown has not been worn in 300 years; the kingdom has been ruled by a circlet of state instead. Halric has been advisor for 8 years and has slowly built influence. The blood comet has been visible 3 weeks; in legend it heralds the death of kings.
worldBible.currentCrisis: Aldric is dying — slowly poisoned by Halric over months. The keep is sealed. Halric is positioning to crown a puppet successor. The blood comet approaches its zenith (4-5 days out). The dream has been waking the player for weeks.
worldBible.themes: Inheritance and refusal. The cost of power. Whether destiny is a gift or a theft. What it means to be chosen versus to choose.

worldConstraints: Magic exists but is rare and costly. The Ember Crown is a true relic — it cannot be lifted by anyone who has not dreamed of it (they burn). Dreams from the Crown are real prophetic events, not metaphor. No teleportation, no resurrection, no instant communication.
adaptationRules: Defaults: (1) NPCs are physical and consistent — no teleportation. (2) Influence, never force — use dreams, encountered NPCs, ambient events; never bend physics. (3) Adapt the objective's FORM, not its existence. (4) The world has memory — NPCs remember player actions. (5) Honor every player choice as real, even disruptive ones.

pacingBudget.raw: 5-7 beats per playthrough. Climax must occur by beat 6-7. The opening beat is hardcoded; the AI generates beats 2 onward.
pacingBudget.tokensRaw: ~1000 output tokens per turn. Resolution: 80-120 words. Beat intro: 150-200 words. Choices: one short sentence each.

characters.name: Sera
characters.physical: Gaunt woman, mid-30s, weather-worn. Silver pin shaped like a flame on her cloak. Sword on her hip. Always slightly travel-stained — the urgency shows.
characters.voice: Terse, mission-focused, brusque urgency. Does not waste words. Uses imperatives. Italics in dialogue rare and meaningful when they happen.
characters.motivations: Get the dreamer to King Aldric in time. Loyal to the dying king's faction; loyal to the crown's rite. Will give her life for the mission.
characters.allegiances: The Old Faction. Sworn to Aldric personally. Distrusts Halric.
characters.startingLocation: At the player's gate, Wren's Hollow.
characters.startingStatus: Alive, healthy, four days' road dust on her.
characters.knowledgeText: Knows the king is dying of poisoning. Knows the dream-mark (can recognize a true dreamer). Does not know specifically that Halric is the poisoner — suspects but cannot prove.
characters.notes: Will not bend rules to find the player if they flee — she searches the village briefly, then rides on. Her competence is the player's leverage; her absence is a real cost.

characters.name: King Aldric
characters.physical: Mid-40s, gaunt now (wasn't before), eyes still sharp when conscious. Wearing simple linen, not regalia. Bedridden, deteriorating fast.
characters.voice: Slow, deliberate, lucid in flashes. The voice of a man who has accepted dying. Compassionate; speaks to the player as an equal, not a subject.
characters.motivations: Pass the Ember Crown to a true dreamer before the comet's zenith, so the rite holds. Save the kingdom from Halric's puppet.
characters.allegiances: The kingdom itself. The crown's rite. His own legitimacy.
characters.startingStatus: Dying. Days, possibly hours. Conscious in flashes.
characters.knowledgeText: Knows he is being poisoned. Knows Halric is responsible. Knows the rite of the crown.
characters.notes: Will likely die in the climactic beat regardless of player path. The QUESTION is whether the player is present, late, or absent — and what they do at the bedside.

characters.name: High Advisor Halric
characters.physical: Tall, gray-haired, late 50s. Dark robes. A cold smile that never reaches his eyes. Always composed; never visibly hurried.
characters.voice: Cold, patient, intelligent. Polite to the point of mockery. Refers to people by formal title. Smiles when delivering bad news.
characters.motivations: Crown a puppet successor and rule through them. Eliminate or co-opt the true dreamer. Consolidate power before the comet passes.
characters.allegiances: Himself. His own faction (a small ring of conspirators in the keep).
characters.startingStatus: Healthy, scheming, increasingly impatient as the comet approaches.
characters.knowledgeText: Knows the crown's rite intimately. Knows the dreamer exists somewhere in the kingdom. Has people searching. Underestimates the player's agency.
characters.notes: Should be reasonable-seeming on first meeting. The horror is in his patience and competence, not in cartoon villainy. The Kingmaker ending hinges on the player choosing to weaponize this against him.

openingBeat.title: I. The Riders
openingBeat.setting: Day 1, dawn, Wren's Hollow. Player at home. Three riders approaching the gate. Blood comet visible in eastern sky.
openingBeat.prose:
You wake to the sound of your own name being called. Outside, dawn is breaking thin and red over Wren's Hollow, and the blood comet hangs low in the east — a long wound across the sky. Hooves on the dirt road. Three riders. The lead one — a gaunt woman with a silver pin shaped like a flame — dismounts at your gate.

You have been dreaming of fire for weeks. A crown that burns the hand that wears it. A king on a bed that smells of ash. The dreams have been getting worse.

She is at your door. Her hand rises to knock.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Open the door before she can knock.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Slip out the back, into the woods.

playerStartingState.knowledgeText: Has been dreaming of fire, a burning crown, and a king on a bed of ash for weeks. Does not know any specifics about who, where, or why. Has not connected the dreams to the comet visible in the sky.
playerStartingState.condition: Well-fed, healthy, sleep-deprived (the dream wakes them).
